section_summary.extract_value: This introduction section reviews theoretical and empirical literature on social safeness, body image, eating psychopathology, and body appreciation. It discusses how social acceptance influences body-related behaviors, the evolution of beauty ideals (particularly thinness in Western societies), the paradoxical effects of dieting in normal-weight individuals, and the protective role of self-compassion and body appreciation in reducing body dissatisfaction and promoting adaptive eating behaviors. No empirical studies are presented or numbered in this section.

section_summary.extract_value: This introduction section establishes the theoretical foundation for a study examining the relationship between social safeness, body appreciation, and disordered eating. The text reviews literature on how social connectedness relates to emotion regulation and well-being, discusses the role of interpersonal contexts in eating psychopathology, and explains how body appreciation may mediate the relationship between social connectedness and eating behaviors. The study aims to test a mediator model in which social safeness and connectedness are negatively linked to disordered eating through mechanisms of emotion regulation, with body appreciation and inflexible eating rules as key mediators.
